CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the effectiveness of recent medication adjustments for generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a mixed response to the recent changes in his treatment regimen. He notes that while there has been a slight reduction in the frequency of his tension-type headaches, now occurring approximately 2 times per week, the intensity has remained moderate, averaging a score of 4 out of 10. Mr. Smith attributes this improvement to the recent increase in his topiramate dosage to 100 mg daily. He continues to manage his work stress through yoga and guided meditation, which he finds beneficial.
Sleep quality has shown some improvement; Mr. Smith reports averaging 6.5 hours of sleep per night with fewer awakenings during the night. However, he still experiences difficulty in falling asleep, which he attributes to racing thoughts related to work. He has been compliant with trazodone and melatonin, but he expresses a desire to explore additional options for sleep management.
Fatigue persists, particularly in the mornings, but Mr. Smith describes a modest improvement in energy levels throughout the day. He reports that the dizziness has resolved entirely, which he attributes to better hydration and reduced screen time during work hours.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 250 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 50 mg at bedtime (consider alternative if sleep issues persist) 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime (continued) 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 6. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 7. Topiramate 100 mg daily (continued) 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, reporting that his workload remains high but he is employing better stress management techniques. He remains physically active and has increased his running frequency, which he finds helps with his overall mood and energy levels. He continues to adhere to a balanced diet and avoids alcohol, while maintaining low caffeine intake.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Anxiety levels stable; improved sleep quality; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Reduced headache frequency; dizziness resolved; no visual disturbances or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue continues, with no fever or weight changes noted.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 118/75 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented, appears well-groomed; mood appears stable with mild anxiety noted. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; no dizziness reported. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with no signs of distress.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 250 mg daily. Monitor for any changes in anxiety levels. Lorazepam usage remains as needed for acute episodes. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone and melatonin; consider a referral to a sleep specialist if sleep disturbances do not improve within the next month. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue topiramate at 100 mg daily; monitor headache frequency and intensity. Continue amitriptyline at 50 mg nightly. Schedule a follow-up in one month to assess response to the current regimen. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage continued engagement in physical activity and mindfulness practices. If fatigue persists or worsens, consider further evaluation for underlying causes.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-05-01 to monitor symptom changes, evaluate treatment efficacy, and discuss any new concerns. Mr. Smith is advised to maintain a headache diary to better track patterns and potential triggers.
